naming: The loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with CamelCaseNamingConvention + IgnoreUnmatchedProperties. A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. The 'operation' enum is parsed case-insensitively with '-'/'_' stripped.

keys.description: The flow's unique identifier; seeds the stable FlowId. A blank value fails: "'name' is required for a cpy flow."

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.
keys.validation: Unknown value fails to load: "<source>: 'mode' has unknown value '<value>'. Allowed: auto, manual, disabled."

keys.description: Optional grouping label recorded with the run.
What the flow does with the matched files: copy each verbatim, bundle them all into one .zip written to the target (zip-only), or extract each matched .zip's entries to the target.

The source of a single copy (with target). One of source/target OR items is required, not both; declaring both fails with "declare either a top-level 'source'/'target' or an 'items' list, not both." A single source/target is the one-copy shortcut for one step.

The source root: a local/UNC path, an Azure Blob/ADLS Gen2 URI (abfss://fs@account.dfs.core.windows.net/path or the https form), or an AWS S3 URI (s3://bucket/prefix). SFTP is a separate flow type (sftp), not a cpy endpoint.
File-name glob selecting which files under the root are copied (BCL FileSystemName glob).
Recurse into subfolders under the source root.
Only copy files modified within this many days; 0 copies everything (the 14-day filter the lake-to-lake runbooks used).
Optional ${...} reference to a connection string authenticating an Azure source. Absent = ambient managed identity (SQLFLOW_AZURE_AUTH).
Optional ${...} reference to a SAS token authenticating an Azure source.
Optional ${...} reference to a storage account key authenticating an Azure source (the shape the legacy runbooks used). Prefer managed identity where the drop zone allows it.
Required ${...} reference to the AWS access key id when the source is an s3:// URI (S3 has no ambient identity); paired with secretKeyRef. Ignored for non-S3 sources.
Required ${...} reference to the AWS secret access key when the source is an s3:// URI; paired with accessKeyRef.
The AWS region of an s3:// source (e.g. eu-west-1). Ignored for non-S3 sources.

Where the files are written. Same shape as source; its selection fields (pattern/recursive/modifiedWithinDays) are ignored. The Azure auth refs (connectionStringRef/sasTokenRef/accountKeyRef) apply to an Azure target; accessKeyRef/secretKeyRef/region apply to an s3:// target.
The target root: a local/UNC path, an Azure storage URI, or an AWS S3 URI (s3://bucket/prefix).

Several source-to-target copies in one pipeline: one entry per file set, each with its own source and target (same shape as the top-level source/target). The alternative to a single source/target; declaring both fails. The flow-level operation and options apply to every entry. Each entry's source is a lineage read node and its target a written node the downstream ingestion reads, so one pipeline copying a whole source system connects every landed folder to its load.
The source of this copy step (same shape as the top-level source).
This step's source root: a local/UNC path, an Azure storage URI, or an AWS S3 URI (s3://bucket/prefix).
File-name glob selecting which files under this step's source are copied.
Recurse into subfolders under this step's source root.
Only copy files modified within this many days for this step; 0 copies everything.
Required ${...} reference to the AWS access key id when this step's source is an s3:// URI; paired with secretKeyRef.
Required ${...} reference to the AWS secret access key when this step's source is an s3:// URI; paired with accessKeyRef.
The AWS region of this step's s3:// source (e.g. eu-west-1).
The target of this copy step (same shape as the top-level target).
This step's target root: a local/UNC path, an Azure storage URI, or an AWS S3 URI (s3://bucket/prefix).
Overwrite an existing target file; when false a collision fails rather than clobbers.
Preserve each file's folder structure (relative to the source root) under the target; flat by name otherwise.

Skip writing a file whose target copy already holds byte-identical content (compared by content hash from one target listing), so an unchanged re-run does not bump the target's modified time and re-trigger downstream ingestion. Set false to rewrite every matched file unconditionally and avoid the comparison cost. No effect when overwrite is false.
The archive name for operation: zip; ignored otherwise.

Optional explicit declaration of a single file set this copy produces, for lineage. A copy's target is its output, so when neither output nor outputs is given lineage binds the single target folder to the downstream ingestion. Declare an output to bind a specific landed folder/pattern to the ingestion(s) that read it. Same shape as a file source's selection. Convenience for the one-folder case; use outputs for several.

The folder, full file path, or Azure/cloud URL this copy lands. An Azure storage URI is canonicalized so its shape (abfss:// vs https .dfs) does not affect the lineage node; a local path is normalized against the estate root. Required when an output block is present.
The file-name glob within output.location (e.g. detail_*.json). Matched with FileSystemName; two wildcard patterns are tested for overlap. Quote a glob beginning with '*'.
An optional regex over the full landing path, applied symmetrically with a consumer's srcPathMask by FileSelection.Feeds, for cases the folder prefix cannot express. An invalid regex fails at parse.

Several file sets this copy produces: one entry per (folder, pattern), each the same shape as output. FlowSetCollector registers the copy as a file producer and reconciles each entry independently against every file ingestion with the shared engine-parity matcher (src/SqlFlow.Core/Files/FileSelection.cs), so a copy that fans several folders connects to each downstream load; a drop nothing consumes still records its own file node. Many files in ONE folder need only a single entry with a glob, since the file node is the folder.
The folder, full file path, or Azure/cloud URL this drop lands at. Same normalization/canonicalization as output.location. Required for each entry.
The file-name glob within this drop's location; same semantics as output.srcFile.
An optional regex over this drop's full landing path; same semantics as output.srcPathMask.
